question: An engineer is performing an ISSU upgrade on the Cisco MDS 9000 Series switch. What is the impact on the control plane of the switch?
options: It is down for less than 80 seconds.
It remains down for more than 80 seconds but less than 140 seconds.
It remains down until the next reboot.
It remains up throughout the update.
theory: An MDS 'install all' nondisruptive software upgrade (ISSU) reloads the supervisor's control-plane software while the data plane keeps forwarding Fibre Channel frames; Cisco documents that this control-plane interruption lasts under about 80 seconds even though the overall install process (which also cycles line cards) takes longer. Understanding this number matters for planning maintenance windows: a nondisruptive upgrade does not mean zero impact - the control plane briefly goes down while the standby supervisor takes over and the previously active one reloads - it only means the fabric keeps switching frames. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 11 - Nondisruptive Upgrade)
